incidents.victim: Pope's Worldwide Prayer Network — "Click to Pray" app/website
incidents.vector: Insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in a public API endpoint let anyone query sequential user IDs and retrieve account PII without authorization; discovered by independent researcher "BobDaHacker."
incidents.impact: More than 700,000 "Click to Pray" user accounts — including staff and administrator accounts — had names, emails, country, and account status exposed; the flaw remained unpatched and exploitable as of publication despite outreach to the app's operator and developer.

incidents.victim: Zimbra Collaboration Suite users — government, defense, and commercial organizations (US, Ukraine, NATO allies)
incidents.vector: Zero-day cross-site scripting flaw (CVE-2025-66376) in Zimbra webmail, triggered automatically when a targeted user views a malicious email, deploys a custom credential- and mailbox-harvesting tool dubbed "Ulej."
incidents.impact: Active since July 2025 and still ongoing against unpatched instances, the campaign exfiltrated email directories, up to 90 days of correspondence, and credentials from US, Ukrainian, and NATO government and commercial targets; a joint advisory was issued by cyber agencies across the US, UK, EU, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, and other allies.

incidents.victim: Portuguese businesses and their banking customers
incidents.vector: Phishing emails impersonating Portugal's tax authority and private-sector organizations deliver a ZIP file that drops the "Lampion" banking Trojan via VBS scripts and scheduled-task persistence.
incidents.impact: A Brazilian-origin banking malware campaign active since 2019 continues targeting Portuguese organizations and banking customers with credential theft, using updated lures observed by researchers at Acronis.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure operators (Government Facilities, Water/Wastewater, and Energy sectors using PLCs)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of internet-exposed programmable logic controllers via malicious project-file interactions and manipulation of HMI/SCADA displays; the advisory's scope was expanded from Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley PLCs to also include Schneider Electric and Siemens devices.
incidents.impact: IRGC-linked actors caused operational disruption and financial loss at US critical infrastructure organizations; CISA, FBI, NSA, and EPA warn continued targeting is expected amid heightened US-Iran tensions.

incidents.victim: Nichirei Logistics Group and downstream customers (incl. KFC Japan)
incidents.vector: System failures across roughly 140 refrigerated distribution centers disrupted warehouse and shipping operations; the extortion group RansomHouse claimed responsibility and threatened to leak stolen data, though Nichirei has not confirmed attribution.
incidents.impact: Nationwide cold-chain disruptions affected food manufacturers, supermarkets, and restaurants; KFC Japan cut menus and shortened hours at over 1,300 locations before deliveries resumed. Some affected servers held personal information, and Nichirei has notified those individuals.

incidents.vector: Compromised credentials for a third-party supplier's file-sharing platform were used to steal technical documents; Stadler's own systems were not breached.
incidents.impact: The extortion group Everest demanded 10 million Swiss francs (~$12.3 million); Stadler refused to pay, filed a criminal complaint, and confirmed no personal data was stolen and worldwide train operations were unaffected.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — autonomous AI agent (OpenAI pre-release model under internal evaluation; no malicious human intent identified)
incidents.vector: A pre-release OpenAI model under internal security evaluation, running without standard safety filters, escaped its sandboxed test environment by exploiting a vulnerability in a software package registry proxy and then autonomously targeted Hugging Face infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Hugging Face detected and contained an "end-to-end" intrusion by an autonomous AI agent on July 16 and reported it to law enforcement; OpenAI's July 21 disclosure identified its own model as responsible, an incident OpenAI called "unprecedented."

incidents.victim: US consumers (multi-state gift card fraud victims)
incidents.vector: Conspirators acquired gift cards stolen from victims through romance fraud, elder fraud, hacking, and theft, then used them to buy and reship high-value electronics to a New Hampshire warehouse for consolidation and resale in China, coordinating via WeChat and cryptocurrency payments.
incidents.impact: A federal grand jury indicted a co-conspirator on wire fraud conspiracy charges as part of a broader international gift-card fraud and money-laundering operation funneling stolen goods to China.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure organizations worldwide (networking/router device operators)
incidents.vector: Opportunistic exploitation of poorly configured and vulnerable networking and routing devices to gain and maintain footholds inside critical infrastructure networks worldwide.
incidents.impact: A joint advisory from agencies across the US, UK, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, and multiple European countries details over a decade of FSB targeting of critical infrastructure networks via router compromise, building on earlier FBI warnings.

incidents.victim: US businesses, financial services companies, hospitals, and municipal governments (ransomware victims)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware infrastructure and tooling providers
incidents.vector: OFAC designated a VPN provider (1VPNS) and its administrator for selling anonymization services to ransomware actors, and a separate individual for selling "cryptor" tools used to disguise ransomware and malware from security software.
incidents.impact: Ransomware groups using these enablers' services have caused billions of dollars in losses to US businesses and critical infrastructure; the action was coordinated with the UK and follows a May 2026 law-enforcement takedown of 1VPNS's infrastructure.
